transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Yeah… I’m here because I can’t seem to stop going back over things at home. The outlets, the locks, my tools, even dust on surfaces—I’ll check or fix something, then I’ll walk away and feel like I didn’t really do it right, so I go back again. And again.

It eats up most of the day sometimes. I get worn out, but I still don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone. I mean, even before coming here I got stuck with the door lock, and then I noticed the little mess by the entryway, and it just… it’s like one thing turns into another.
Do you find that your mind keeps going back to certain thoughts or images that bother you, even if you try to push them away?

Yeah, they do. Like, even if I know I did the job right, my head won’t leave it alone. I’ll get this thought that maybe there’s a loose wire I missed and the house is going to burn down, or maybe I left a nail somewhere and my wife’s going to step on it or get hurt.

And I try to tell myself, no, I checked it, I did it right… but then the thought comes back louder. It’s like trying not to think about it makes it stick more. I know that sounds kind of—well, I used to be careful with tools, my dad was big on that, “put everything back where it belongs,” you know—but this feels different. It just keeps jumping back in.
When you go back to check things like the locks or outlets, are you trying to prevent something bad from happening, like a fire or someone breaking in?

Yeah, I mean… I go back because I can’t leave it alone. The outlets, the locks, my tools, even little dust or messes in the house—I keep checking or fixing them over and over.

Sometimes I’ll think I’m done, then I’m halfway across the room and it’s like, no, I need to look again. And then that turns into another thing. Like if I’m checking the lock, I notice the tool bench, or the dust on the table, and suddenly I’ve lost hours. My wife says I disappear into it, and I guess I do.

By the end I’m worn out, but I still don’t feel sure enough to just stop.
When you go back to check things like the locks or outlets, does it help calm the worry in your mind, at least for a little while?

For a minute, maybe, yeah. Like I’ll check the outlet or the lock and think, okay, that’s done… but then I’m already looking at it again, or I notice the tools aren’t sitting quite right, or there’s dust on something.

It’s not even like I feel good after. It’s more like I’m trying to get to that feeling of “okay, now I can leave it,” but I don’t really get there. I just keep going back over the same stuff until I’m exhausted. My wife will be doing something normal, like making coffee, and I’m still stuck by the door or the workbench, checking and fixing the same thing again.
Do these thoughts ever feel like they don’t really belong to you, like they’re intrusive or unwanted, even though they keep coming back?

Yeah… unwanted, definitely. They don’t feel like something I’m choosing to think about. It’s more like they barge in.

Like I can know I did the wiring right, I can remember checking it, but then this ugly thought pops in that maybe I missed one loose wire and the whole house is going to burn down. Or that I left a nail somewhere and my wife’s going to step on it. And I’ll try to push it away, tell myself I’m being ridiculous, but then it comes back even stronger.

It’s strange because I’ve always been a careful guy—my dad taught me that with tools, measure twice, clean up after yourself, all that—but this isn’t just being careful. It feels like my own brain won’t leave me alone.

Do these unwanted thoughts lead you to do things over and over in a specific way, like checking or arranging items, because you feel you have to in order to feel okay or to prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah, I do. It’s like… I feel like I have to go back and do it again, even if I just did it.

That’s pretty much why I’m here, honestly. I spend most of my day going over the same outlets, locks, tools, dust in the house… checking them, fixing them, straightening things, wiping at stuff. And then I’ll think, okay, that’s enough, but it doesn’t feel enough.

My dad used to keep his garage spotless, you know, and he’d get on me about putting tools back where they belong—though that was different, I guess. This is more like I can’t move on. I’ll go to leave the room and then turn around again because something doesn’t feel right. And by the time I stop, I’m worn out, but I still don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone.
Do you feel like things have to be arranged or done in a very specific, exact way, not just to be safe, but to feel right or to prevent a bad feeling?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not only safety, though safety is part of it. It’s more like if the tools aren’t sitting right, or I see dust somewhere, or I look at the outlet and it just doesn’t feel settled, I can’t leave it.

I mean, I’m here because I spend most of my day going back over the same stuff—the outlets, the locks, the tools, dust around the house—checking it, fixing it, then checking it again. My wife will say, “You already did that,” and I know I did, but it still feels wrong.

It’s like when my dad used to get after me about the garage, everything had its place… but this is different. This takes over. I keep doing it until I’m worn out, and even then I don’t really feel sure enough to walk away.

Do these thoughts and the time you spend checking and fixing things interfere with your ability to do other important things in your life, like work, spending time with family, or doing things you enjoy?

Yeah… it does. I mean, it’s embarrassing to say, but I don’t really take paid carpentry jobs anymore. I used to do that, and I was good at it. I liked working with my hands, you know—my dad always said a man should know how to fix what’s in front of him, and I used to help out on community projects too, little repairs, building things for people.

But now the house kind of takes over my whole day. I’ll mean to do one thing, and then I’m still stuck checking or fixing something hours later. By the time I could go out or do anything useful, I’m exhausted.

My wife’s had to pick up a lot more of the errands and decisions too, because I get stuck. She’ll ask me something simple, and I can’t even get to it because I’m wrapped up in whatever I’m checking. So yeah… it’s gotten in the way a lot.
Do you feel that these checks or fixes have to be done in a very specific way or number of times, or else something bad will happen or you won’t feel right?

Yeah… not always a set number, exactly, but it has to feel done the right way. Like I’ll check the outlet, then the lock, then the tools, and if I walk away and it doesn’t feel right, I’m back there again.

It’s most of my day now, honestly—going over the same outlets, locks, tools, dust in the house, checking and fixing them again and again. I’ll think I’m finished, but then I notice one thing off, or I just get that feeling, and I can’t leave it alone.

My dad used to be real particular about tools being put back right, and I guess that sticks in my head sometimes, but this is… more than that. I keep going until I’m worn out, and even then I’m still not sure enough to just let it be.
